reason: The cited evidence supports that nanoscale chemical fluctuations/CSRO are common in CCAs (E1) and that spinodal decomposition and CSRO can occur during aging in MPEAs (E2, E3). However, none of the cited passages involve Mg-containing alloys, address corrosion/oxidation resistance, or link CSRO to protective phase formation versus intermetallic degradation, leaving several key premises unsupported by the specific evidence provided.
premises: Nanoscale chemical fluctuations/CSRO are common in CCAs/MPEAs due to high configurational entropy
Spinodal decomposition and CSRO can occur during aging of MPEAs and contribute to strengthening
CSRO domains can serve as precursors to intermetallic precipitation
The balance between finely dispersed protective phases and coarsened intermetallic networks controls corrosion/oxidation resistance
Mg concentration variations within CSRO domains dictate whether protective phases or intermetallics form
